summary: This article explains how simple board games played with seeds and holes in the sand have tested players' strategy and skill across the Arab world and Africa for centuries, with no dice and no luck involved.
introduce: Show the title “Traditional Board Games of the Region” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: a careful plan for reaching a goal
very, very old; from long ago

challengeTerms.def: easy for anyone to use, reach, or take part in
to work something out carefully, often with numbers or steps
customs, art, and traditions passed down from earlier generations

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a simple game with no fancy pieces can be just as fun as an expensive one? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why strategy matters more than luck in this ancient game.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review strategy, capture, and ancient, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses accessible, calculate, and heritage to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
